subject: PayLane: sudden p95/p99 spikes + 429 surge after retry rollout
messages:
From: Jordan Park <jordan@paylane.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: eng-ops@paylane.com, Emma Li <emma.li@paylane.com>
Date: 2026-08-15 09:12 -0700
Subject: Sudden spikes on p95/p99 after our retry rollout — seeing 429s and timeouts

Kim,

We rolled our client-side retry policy to prod at 05:30 PT (simple fixed 1s backoff, 3 retries) and immediately started seeing huge p95/p99 regressions for the Redwood Hosted API. Datadog shows a cluster of 429s and a big spike in tail latency that correlates with our retry wave. Our product is timing out in customer flows.

Attached: paylane-datadog-timeseries.png and a small sample of request IDs (request-ids-20260815.txt).

Can you confirm this is on your side? We need a fast mitigation — can you suggest a short-term configuration we can apply while we revert? We’re also open to a temporary capacity reservation.

Jordan
Lead SRE, PayLane

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Park <jordan@paylane.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-15 09:28 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden spikes on p95/p99 after our retry rollout — seeing 429s and timeouts

Jordan — thanks for the quick heads up and for the attachments. I see the Datadog snapshot you sent. I’ve looped in Rishi (runtime) and Marcus (ops).

Immediate next steps we can do from our side:
- Turn on a per-tenant soft-rate-limit for PayLane traffic (low-risk, non-disruptive) to prevent retry amplification.
- Temporarily increase your burst quota on the hosted tier for the next 72 hours to absorb retries while you revert.
- Enable detailed request-level tracing for the suspect window and ask you for additional request IDs if available.

Can you confirm the time window you rolled (05:30 PT) and if you have a replay fixture for the requests? We’ll aim for a mitigation action within 45 minutes.

If you’re available, I can open a quick 30-min bridge — we’ll invite runtime and SRE.

—Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Jordan Park <jordan@paylane.com>
Cc: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-15 09:50 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden spikes on p95/p99 after our retry rollout — seeing 429s and timeouts

Jordan / Kim — quick update from runtime: we’re seeing a clear pattern where a cohesive burst of retries is driving down available serving slots, which in turn increases queueing and p99. The 429s are coming from our per-request rate limiter hitting token exhaustion; because retries come right after 429s, the client wave re-submits and amplifies the congestion.

What we’ve done so far (09:45 PT):
- Enabled a per-tenant debounce window: for repeated identical request signatures from PayLane, we’ll suppress accept attempts for 500ms after a 429. This is experimental but should substantially cut amplification.
- Pushed a temporary +25% burst quota for PayLane for 72 hours.
- Turned on additional KV-cache warming for common prefixes in your traffic pattern.

Ask from PayLane: full request-ids for 09:30-10:00 PT and an example request JSON to validate signature deduping. Also please apply an exponential backoff client-side (we recommend jittered expo starting at 200ms) before rolling back fully.

We’ll monitor p95/p99 for the next 2 hours and can escalate to a dedicated pool if this doesn’t stabilize.

—Rishi
Sr. Applied ML Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Park <jordan@paylane.com>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: eng-ops@paylane.com, Emma Li <emma.li@paylane.com>
Date: 2026-08-15 10:05 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden spikes on p95/p99 after our retry rollout — seeing 429s and timeouts

Thanks Rishi — confirming we can supply the requested sample. We don’t have expo backoff currently; we used fixed 1s between retries to keep implementation simple. We’ll pause the rollout immediately and revert to the previous client during the revert window (ETA 60m).

Attaching perf-snapshot-1623.json with a sample request body and the request-ids file. We’ll stand by for your observability notes.

Jordan

From: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Jordan Park <jordan@paylane.com>
Cc: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-15 13:10 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden spikes on p95/p99 after our retry rollout — seeing 429s and timeouts

Quick ops note (13:05 PT): after Rishi’s temporary tweaks we saw a 68% drop in 429 rate for PayLane in the first 30 minutes and p99 decreased by ~40% on the affected endpoints. We’re continuing to watch.

Follow-up actions I’ve taken:
- Left the per-tenant debounce in place for another 18 hours.
- Set up an automated alert to page on recurrence in the 15m window.
- Created a short-term Play: route PayLane to the Dedicated-burst pool if error-rate rises above 2.5% sustained for 5 minutes (will require exec approval for capacity cost).

Monica will assemble the telemetry pack for your postmortem with timestamps and request IDs.

—Marcus
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Emma Li <emma.li@paylane.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Jordan Park <jordan@paylane.com>
Cc: eng-ops@paylane.com, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-17 16:40 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden spikes on p95/p99 after our retry rollout — seeing 429s and timeouts

Hey team — quick wrap from PayLane: after reverting the client rollout and taking your recommendations (expo backoff + small jitter) we’ve not seen a recurrence. The customers who saw failures initially are now recovering and we’re pulling together an internal RCA.

Request for exec update: our VP Product would like a short note for the leadership call tomorrow summarizing root cause, what Redwood did (debounce + burst quota), and next steps for prevention (server-side Retry-After headers, more prominent guidance in the retry docs, and a dedicated onboarding checklist for heavy-traffic customers).

Jordan and I will sync with Kim to get the leadership note. Thanks for the rapid response.

—Emma Li
Customer Success, PayLane
